title: Wrapped up in fear, and called by name.
subtitle: The call that came after the silence
then: After the first revelation in the cave of Hira, there was a pause. Then, walking one day, the Prophet ﷺ heard a voice from the sky and saw the same angel {trap}between the sky and the earth{/trap}. Shaken, he went home and said: wrap me up. {idea}Then these verses came{/idea}, and revelation became strong and continuous.
now: You got the job, the diagnosis, the new baby, the responsibility you prayed for. And you are scared stiff, hiding under a blanket at three in the afternoon. {idea}Fear does not cancel the call.{/idea} You can be shaking and still be the one chosen.
old: If I am this afraid, maybe I am not meant for this.
new: Even the Prophet ﷺ was shaken, and the call still came to him, by name.
try: Name the thing you are afraid to start, and ask Allah for help with it before tonight.

title: Get up and warn. The blanket was never the plan.
subtitle: From prophet to messenger in two words
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}prepare to go forth with zeal and warn the people{/idea}. With this the Prophet ﷺ became a messenger, just as he became a prophet with the first revelation, Read. From the blanket to the public square of Makkah.
now: You know something your friend needs to hear. A warning about the bad deal, the bad crowd, the habit that is quietly ruining them. {trap}You keep saying it is not your place.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the kind thing is to get up and say it.{/idea}
old: It is not my business to tell anyone they are heading the wrong way.
new: Caring for people sometimes means standing up and warning them, gently and clearly.
try: Send one honest, kind message today to someone you have been afraid to caution.

title: Make your Lord the biggest thing in your eyes.
subtitle: Allahu Akbar as the first instruction
then: He had just been told to go out and warn a hostile city. The next word was to {idea}declare the greatness of his Lord{/idea}. Before facing the chiefs of Quraysh, he was to see who was truly great.
now: The meeting with the boss. The landlord. The exam board. The bill. They fill the whole screen of your mind. {idea}Allahu Akbar is not only words in prayer.{/idea} It resizes everything else.
old: This problem is the biggest thing in my life right now.
new: My Lord is greater, so every problem is smaller than it looks.
try: Before your hardest task today, say Allahu Akbar slowly three times and mean it.

title: Keep your clothes clean, inside and out.
subtitle: Purity of body, earning, heart and character
then: The scholars read it in layers. Ibn Sirin said {idea}clean them with water{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said do not wear clothes {trap}bought from unlawful earnings{/trap}. Said bin Jubayr said purify your heart and intentions. Al-Hasan said beautify your character.
now: The shirt is ironed for the interview. But what paid for it? And what is your heart aiming at when you walk in? {reward}Clean clothes, clean money, a clean intention, kind manners.{/reward} The messenger had to carry all four.
old: Being clean means looking neat and fresh.
new: Purity reaches from my clothes to my money, my motives and my manners.
try: Check one thing you own today: was it earned cleanly? If unsure, give something in charity.

title: Walk away from the idols.
subtitle: Leaving what people worship besides Allah
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said {trap}Ar-Rujz means the idols{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ was told to keep away from them, in a city where they surrounded the Kabah and shaped daily life.
now: No one you know bows to a statue. But the follower count, the brand, the paycheck, the approval of the in-crowd can start making the decisions. {idea}Whatever you obey over Allah is the thing to walk away from.{/idea}
old: Idols are an ancient thing that has nothing to do with me.
new: Anything I put above Allah's word is the rujz I am told to leave.
try: Notice one thing that pulls you away from prayer today, and step away from it once.

title: Give without expecting to get more back.
subtitle: A gift is not an investment
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}do not give a gift seeking more than it in return{/trap}. Mujahid read it another way: {idea}do not grow weak in seeking more good{/idea}. A messenger gives everything and does not keep a tab on people.
now: You helped your cousin move flat. You lent the money. You covered the shift. And now you are quietly keeping score, waiting to be paid back with interest. {reward}A gift with a hook is not a gift.{/reward}
old: When I do someone a favour, they owe me one.
new: I give for Allah, so nobody owes me, and I can keep doing good.
try: Do one favour today and tell no one, and expect nothing for it.

title: Be patient, and let the patience be for your Lord.
subtitle: Patience with a direction
then: Mujahid said: make your patience with their harms be {idea}for the Face of your Lord{/idea}. Ibrahim An-Nakhai said: be patient in your giving for the sake of Allah. The mission had barely begun, and he was already being told what it would cost.
now: The colleague who belittles you in meetings. The relative who never says thank you. You grit your teeth and survive. {reward}That same patience, turned toward Allah, becomes worship.{/reward}
old: I am only putting up with this because I have no choice.
new: I bear it for my Lord, so not a moment of it is wasted.
try: When something irritates you today, whisper: for You, my Lord, and let it pass.

title: When the Trumpet is sounded.
subtitle: The one sound everyone will hear
then: Many early scholars said Naqur is {idea}the Trumpet{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ asked how he could be at ease while the one with the horn waits to be commanded. When the Companions asked what to do, he ﷺ told them to say: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Trustee{/reward}.
now: A fire alarm in the office. Everyone stops, looks up, grabs their things. {idea}One sound and the whole building changes.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ did not answer that thought with panic. He gave his Companions a sentence of trust.
old: Thinking about the end of the world just makes me anxious.
new: The Trumpet is real, and the answer to it is trust, not panic.
try: Say Hasbunallahu wa nimal wakil three times today when something worries you.

title: That Day will be a hard day.
subtitle: A day not like other days
then: Ibn Kathir says hard here means {trap}severe{/trap}. He records that Zurarah bin Awfa, the judge of Basrah, led the morning prayer with this surah. On reaching these verses, {idea}he moaned and fell down dead{/idea}. That is how heavy these words felt to those who heard them truly.
now: You have had hard days. The phone call from the hospital. The day you lost the job. You know how a day can be harder than the others. {idea}You were warned about this one, and the warning is a mercy.{/idea}
old: Hard days just happen to me and I cannot prepare.
new: This hard Day was named in advance so I can get ready while it is easy.
try: Write down one thing you want to have done before that Day, and start it today.

title: Not easy for those who denied it.
subtitle: The hard Day is not hard for everyone

row.title: the deniers
sub: it will not be easy for them

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}it will not be easy for them{/trap}, like the verse where the disbelievers say: this is a hard day. The verse names who it is hard for, which {reward}leaves hope for those who believed{/reward}.
now: Two students walk into the same exam. One studied all term, one did not. The paper is the same. {idea}How hard it feels depends on what you did before it.{/idea}
old: Judgement Day will be equally terrifying for all of us.
new: Its hardness falls on denial, so belief now is how I make it easier.
try: Renew your belief today: say the shahadah slowly and think about each part.

title: Leave Me with the one I created alone.
subtitle: He came into the world with nothing
then: Ibn Kathir names him as {trap}Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah{/trap}, a chief of Quraysh. Allah reminds him that he came out of his mother's womb {idea}alone, without wealth or children{/idea}. Everything after that was a gift.
now: Your title, your car, your house, the people who answer when you call. It is easy to tell the story as if you made it all. {idea}You arrived with nothing.{/idea} Every line since then was given.
old: I worked for everything I have, nobody gave me anything.
new: I was created alone with nothing, so all I have is a gift from Him.
try: List three things you have today that you did not have at birth, and thank Allah for each.

title: Then I gave him wealth that kept on spreading.
subtitle: Abundance as a test
then: Allah recounts His favours to the man who called the Quran magic. {reward}Wealth vast and abundant{/reward}, says Ibn Kathir. Notice the wording: {idea}I granted him{/idea}. Allah calls it His gift, even to someone who would deny Him.
now: Payday hits your account. A bonus. A good month for the business. {idea}Notice who the verse says gave it.{/idea} The money that pays your rent is a gift with a question attached: what will you do with Me now?
old: My income is the result of my skill and nothing else.
new: Every bit of wealth I hold, Allah granted, and He watches what it does to me.
try: On your next payday, give a small part away first, before spending anything.

title: And sons who stayed by his side.
subtitle: Family close by is a blessing too
then: Mujahid said his sons {reward}were not absent{/reward}. Servants and workers handled trade, so the sons sat with their father and he enjoyed their company. Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}a great blessing{/idea}, given to a man who answered it with denial.
now: Sunday lunch with everyone at the table. Your kids still living nearby. A parent who picks up on the first ring. {idea}It feels ordinary, and it is one of the biggest gifts you have.{/idea}
old: Having family around is just normal, nothing special.
new: Family close by is a gift from Allah that deserves gratitude, not blindness.
try: Call or sit with one family member today and thank Allah for them afterwards.

title: I smoothed his whole life out before him.
subtitle: When everything is easy, watch your heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah made it possible for him to {reward}amass wealth, luxuries and more{/reward}. Yet he met these blessings with {trap}ingratitude and rejection of Allah's signs{/trap}, after knowing them well.
now: The commute is easy, the fridge is full, the kids are healthy, the visa came through. {trap}When life goes smoothly, it is easy to stop needing Allah.{/trap} {idea}The smooth road is the moment to thank Him most.{/idea}
old: When life is easy, I do not really need to pray as hard.
new: Ease is paved by Allah, so the smoother life is, the more thanks I owe.
try: Pick one easy part of your life today and pray two units of thanks for it.
